newsitem.title: USA: New England utilities report scattered outages.
newsitem.headline: New England utilities report scattered outages.

text.p: Two days of heavy rain and high winds have caused scattered power outages and local flooding in southern New England, spokesmen for utilities and municipal officials said Wednesday.
The National Weather Service said the hardest hit areas were in southern New England with eastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island bearing the brunt of the storm.
Boston Edison reported scattered outages throughout the city, affecting some 5,000 residential and commercial customers.

Eastern Utilities, which serves parts of Rhode Island and Connecticut, also reported about 2,500 customers without service. "We lost two feeder cables over night. The first at 4:40 a.m. and the second at 5:30 a.m.," said spokeswoman Elaine Hunt. She said crews were out working to restore power.

The National Weather Service reported the largest accumulation of rain from its station in Blue Hill in Milton, Mass. just south of Boston where 4.6 inches has fallen. Wind gusts of 53 mph, strong enough to qualify as tropical storm strength, were also reported at that station.
"We expect continued heavy rainfall throughout the day," said weather service spokesman Jim Notchey. "But the rain should end by dark."
In addition, flooding has caused service delays on the city's subway system and brought traffic to a snail's pace, city transportation officials.

Commonwealth Electric Co, a subsidiary of Commonwealth Energy System which provides service to Cape Cod, also reported "a few thousand customers without power," according to spokesman Peter Dimond. "The hardest hit area appears to be Woods Hole in Falmouth where customers have been without power since 3:15 this morning," he said.
